record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Does there exist δ > 0 such that every separable L1,1+ε-space with ε ≤ δ is isomorphic to an L1(ν)-space, and if so does the optimal isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0? Likewise, does there exist δ > 0 such that every (1+ε)-complemented subspace of L1[0,1] with ε ≤ δ is isomorphic to an L1(ν)-space, and if so does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. ([4]) (i) Does there exist a δ > 0 such that every separable L1,1+ε-space is isomorphic to an L1(ν) for ε ≤ δ? If yes then does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0? (ii) Does there exist a δ > 0 such that every (1 + ε)- complemented subspace of L1 is isomorphic to an L1(ν) for ε ≤ δ? If yes then does the isomorphism constant tend to 1 as ε → 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $L_1=L_1[0,1]$ denote the classical Lebesgue space of integrable functions on $[0,1]$, and for a (positive, $\sigma$-finite) measure $\nu$ let $L_1(\nu)$ denote the corresponding $L_1$-space. For $\lambda\ge 1$, a separable Banach space $X$ is called an $\mathcal{L}_{1,\lambda}$-space if every finite-dimensional subspace $E\subset X$ is contained in a finite-dimensional subspace $F\subset X$ for which the Banach–Mazur distance $d(F,\ell_1^{\dim F})\le\lambda$. A closed subspace $Y$ of a Banach space $Z$ is called $\lambda$-complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection $P:Z\to Y$ with $\|P\|\le\lambda$. The Banach–Mazur isomorphism constant between two isomorphic Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ is $d(X,Y)=\inf\{\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|:T:X\to Y\text{ is a linear isomorphism}\}$.

Problem. 
(i) Does there exist $\delta>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\delta]$, every separable $\mathcal{L}_{1,1+\varepsilon}$-space is linearly isomorphic to some space of the form $L_1(\nu)$? If so, can the optimal isomorphism constant $d(X,L_1(\nu))$ be made to tend to $1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, uniformly over all separable $\mathcal{L}_{1,1+\varepsilon}$-spaces $X$?

(ii) Does there exist $\delta>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\delta]$, every $(1+\varepsilon)$-complemented subspace of $L_1[0,1]$ is linearly isomorphic to some space of the form $L_1(\nu)$? If so, does the optimal isomorphism constant tend to $1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, uniformly over all such subspaces?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a resolution of either part. Related quantitative work on $(1+\varepsilon)$-complemented, $(1+\varepsilon)$-isomorphic copies of $L_1$ in dual Banach spaces has appeared recently, but it does not establish the asked-for $\delta>0$ for separable $\mathcal{L}_{1,1+\varepsilon}$-spaces or for $(1+\varepsilon)$-complemented subspaces of $L_1[0,1]$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: (1+)-complemented, (1+)-isomorphic copies of L_1 in dual Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes when a dual Banach space contains, for every ε>0, a (1+ε)-complemented, (1+ε)-isomorphic copy of L_1, but does not resolve the near-isometric L_{1,1+ε} classification question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent quantitative results on near-isometric copies of L_1 do not address the stated δ-question, suggesting the problem remains open.
